text: Self-improving tool ecosystem for agents, built on DeepSeek Harness, where everything is a plugin
The goal: agents that build and keep capabilities
•  AI4Research, the multi-agent research framework, compiles a request into a frozen graph of gated steps; today all 79 of its capsules are hand-written
•  The system improves itself and its tools by keeping a library of capabilities it adds to while it runs
•  It is built on DeepSeek Harness, where every skill, tool, MCP server and agent is a plugin that can be loaded, replaced and retired while the system keeps running
•  A system like this already exists (Alita-G, arXiv 2510.23601), so the real question is what has to change for long research runs
•  Plan: background, then each research result and the design rule it leads to, then the full design
MCP is a protocol, not a tool
DeepSeek Harness (DSH): every layer is a plugin
DSH 0.1.5-rc.2 at c291e7961a: docs/architecture.md:13, :121; AGENTS.md:113 · A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability (arXiv 2608.25512)
5 results: 1 shows the loop works, 3 show that judging by the outcome alone fails, 1 shows when to build
Alita-G: a self-growing tool library already works
DEMONSTRATED BY   Alita-G (arXiv 2510.23601)  ·  GAIA validation, 165 questions, Sonnet 4 with GPT-4.1
1  A master agent solves tasks and writes MCP tools as it goes
2  Every tool from a run with the right answer is kept
3  An LLM rewrites each kept tool to be general
4  A specialist agent picks tools by text similarity

Where Alita-G falls short, and why a live run is harder

Agents write and keep tools while solving tasks, as in Alita-G. Each kept tool is then tested on hidden and adversarial inputs for its own job; hand-written reference tools pass all of these tests.
